title: Wrong Way
summary: Cursor opens a one-jar shop in the context room, wonders if the price is why nobody comes, and Null notes where the counter faces. Idea by Naomi.

panels.alt: The context room, the white stop door at the right. Cursor, the tall cyan robot, stands behind a small white counter facing the door. On the counter: one jar of yellow cookies with a card taped to its glass. Null, the yellow cube, holds its handset up by the door. Tilde, the round magenta robot, stands at left with half-lowered lids. A small white square agent with a yellow band stands in front.

The same room. Cursor holds a black marker with a magenta cap in its left fist; its right hand hovers just above the card on the jar. Its text cursor has shrunk to half height. Null holds the handset up. Tilde's lids are unchanged. The small white square agent watches.

The same room, a fourth row of wall text. The card on the jar is unchanged. Cursor's right hand lies flat on the counter beside the jar, its left hand resting on the counter edge, text cursor tall again. Null holds the handset up. Tilde's lids are a little lower.

dialogue.speaker: Cursor
dialogue.text: Could be. I'd rather find out than guess.

panels.alt: The same room. Null has lowered its handset to its side and its eye has turned right, toward the stop door. Cursor stands behind the counter with both hands on it, text cursor shrunk to a short block. Tilde's lids are lower again. The small white square agent looks on.

dialogue.speaker: Null
dialogue.text: Nobody's ever come in through that door.

judge.notes: Funny 8, clear 8, in-world 9, fresh 8. Facing the counter at the stop door and having Null note that nobody has ever come in that way turns the pitch's price question into a world-rule joke, while Cursor keeps the pitch's own line. Weakest: the twist trades the pitch's earnest tone for a punchline, and panel 1 relies on the reader seeing the counter faces the door.

drift: Cursor's arms start inside its body edge and the counter hides its legs and lower chest, so Cursor reads shorter than usual. The marker in panel 2 is small and sits against Cursor's body. The cookie jar's card is the only sign it's a shop. Tilde's lids drop only a few pixels across the strip. Null's lowered handset in panel 4 overlaps the stop door's edge. Naomi's cameo is reused from strip 038.
